# Theme: Medicaid

```{r}
# first things first, lets create our custom mediciad theme, to reuse for all our plots
# the main goal of mediciad_color palette is to differentiate between expansion and nonexpansion states
# expansion = blue, nonexpansion = red
# we will also include colors for specific outcomes, although TBD if they will get used
# insurance coverage = teal, financial burden = purple
medicaid_colors <- list(
  expansion = "#0342A1",
  expansion_cont = c("#0B81D2", "#0053B1", "#0342A1", "#002880", "#011B5B"),
  
  nonexpansion = "#C6010B",
  nonexpansion_cont = c("#FD2640", "#E80016",  "#C6010B", "#A00002", "#6D0100"),
  
  expansion_state = c("#0342A1","#C6010B")
)
```

```{r}
# reusable function to help us format the color palette and return the correct number
# of colors/shades
medicaid_palette <- function(palette = "categorical", n = NULL, reverse = FALSE) {
  pal <- medicaid_colors[[palette]]
  if (reverse) pal <- rev(pal)
  if (!is.null(n)) {
    if (n <= length(pal)) {
      pal <- pal[1:n]
    }
    else {
      pal <- colorRampPalette(pal)(n)
    }
  }
  return(pal)
}
```

```{r}
# for color scales (scatter plots, line plots, etc)
scale_color_medicaid <- function(palette = "categorical", reverse = FALSE, ...) {
    pal <- medicaid_palette(palette = palette, reverse = reverse)
    ggplot2::discrete_scale(
      "colour",
      paste0("medicaid_", palette),
      palette = function(n) pal[1:n],
      ...
  )
}

# for fill scales (bars, density, areas, boxplots etc)
scale_fill_medicaid <- function(palette = "categorical", reverse = FALSE, ...) {
  pal <- medicaid_palette(palette = palette, reverse = reverse)
  ggplot2::discrete_scale(
    "fill",
    paste0("medicaid_", palette),
    palette = function(n) pal[1:n],
    ...
  )
}
```

```{r}
# now lets create a wrapper for our theme so we can easily add the layer to the plots
theme_medicaid <- function() {
  theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(color = "black", family = font_title, size = 30, face = "italic"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "black", family = font_title, size = 18, face = "italic"),
      axis.title = element_text(color = "black", family = font_body, size = 12),
      axis.text = element_text(color = "black", family = font_data, size = 10),
      legend.title = element_text(color = "black", family = font_body, size = 12, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(color = "black", family = font_data, size = 10),
    )
}
```

```{r}
# now lets do some datat cleaning and wrangling
acs <- acs |>
  # first, filter by working age adults (18-64)
  # next, remove any rows with NA income-to-poverty ratio values and subject weights (we need those)
  # finally, lets only look at US states, so excluding US territories of PR and DC (sorry)
  filter(AGEP >= 18, AGEP <= 64, !is.na(POVPIP), !is.na(PWGTP), state_name != "Puerto Rico", state_name != "District of Columbia") |> 
  mutate(
    # now, lets update the following to be based on 0/1 instead of 2/1 (like acs originally had it)
    insured  = ifelse(HICOV == 1, 1, 0),
    uninsured = ifelse(HICOV == 2, 1, 0),
    privcov = ifelse(PRIVCOV == 1, 1, 0),
    pubcov  = ifelse(PUBCOV == 1, 1, 0),
    # lets create new columns to identify our expansion vs nonexpansion states
    expansion = ifelse(state_name %in% non_expansion, 0, 1),
    expansion_name = ifelse(state_name %in% non_expansion, "Non-Expansion", "Expansion"),
    # lets create a new column to identify those equal or under 138% FPL
    low_income = ifelse(POVPIP <= 138, 1, 0),
    # make sure povert-to-income rartio and subject weights are numeric values for calcs later on
    POVPIP = as.numeric(POVPIP),
    PWGTP  = as.numeric(PWGTP),
  )
```

# Plot: Ranking States by Insured Rate

```{r}
# for ranking states by insured rates,
# lets first filter by low income (<= 138% FPL)
# group by state and then calculate the insured rate for each state
state_rank <- acs_2023 |>
  filter(low_income == 1) |> 
  group_by(state_name) |>
  summarise(
    insured_rate = weighted.mean(insured, PWGTP),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(insured_rate)) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number())

# now that we have our state rankings, we need to add back in our
# expansion type (expansion vs non-expansion) so we can color-code the state icons
rank_tbl <- state_rank |>
  left_join(
    acs |> distinct(state_name, expansion_name),
    by = "state_name"
  )

# create directory so we can save the state icons
dir.create("state_icons", showWarnings = FALSE)

# using usmap and sf libraries to create state icons (for use in the gt table)
states_sf <- usmap::us_map(regions = "states")
sf::st_geometry(states_sf) <- "geom"
states_sf <- st_as_sf(states_sf)

# combine our state rankings with the state icons
states_sf <- states_sf |>
  left_join(rank_tbl |> select(state_name, expansion_name),
            by = c("full" = "state_name"))

# create file names for saving the state icon images
safe_name <- function(x) gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x)

# loop through each state, creating and saving the state icon image for each
for (i in seq_len(nrow(states_sf))) {
  # full state name and expansion status, for this loop
  nm <- states_sf$full[i]
  status <- states_sf$expansion_name[i]

  # if expansion status is blank, skip to next state
  if (is.na(status)) next

  # determine state icon color (blue or red) based on expansion status
  fill_color <- if (status == "Expansion") {
    medicaid_colors$expansion
  } else {
    medicaid_colors$nonexpansion
  }

  # save the color-coded state icon, so we can use it later for the state ranking table
  fn <- file.path("state_icons", paste0(safe_name(nm), ".png"))
  # png(filename = fn, width = 180, height = 120, bg = "transparent")
  # par(mar = rep(0, 4))
  # plot(
  #   st_geometry(states_sf[i, ]),
  #   col = fill_color,
  #   border = NA,
  #   axes = FALSE
  # )
  # dev.off()
}

# now that we have our state icon pngs, lets add them to our ranking df
rank_tbl <- rank_tbl |>
  mutate(
    insured_rate = percent(insured_rate, accuracy = 0.1),
    icon_path = file.path("state_icons", paste0(safe_name(state_name), ".png"))
  ) |>
  arrange(rank) |>
  select(rank, icon_path, state_name, insured_rate, expansion_name)

# now use gt library to make the final, poster-ready ranking table
gt(rank_tbl) |>
  # four columns: rank, color-coded state icon, state name, insured rate (%)
  cols_label(
    rank = "Rank",
    icon_path = "",
    state_name = "State",
    insured_rate = "Insured Rate"
  ) |>
  # since we color the state icons by expansion status, lets hide the expansion status column
  cols_hide(columns = expansion_name) |>
  # add the state icon pngs
  text_transform(
    locations = cells_body(columns = icon_path),
    fn = function(x) {
      local_image(filename = x, height = 18)
    }
  ) |>
  # adjust column names format
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = rank)
  ) |>
  # format font and remove column / row lines 
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(12),
    column_labels.font.weight = "600",
    data_row.padding = px(4),
    table.border.top.style = "hidden",
    table.border.bottom.style = "hidden",
    table_body.hlines.style = "hidden",
    table_body.border.top.style = "hidden",
    table_body.border.bottom.style = "hidden"
  )
```

# Plot: Personograph of Uninsured Rates by State

```{r}
# to create the personograph, we need to calculate the uninsured rates for
# the low income population (<= 138% FPL)
state_personograph <- acs_2023 |>
  filter(low_income == 1) |> 
  group_by(state_name, expansion) |>
  summarize(
    uninsured_rate = weighted.mean(uninsured, PWGTP),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    uninsured_rate = uninsured_rate,
    expansion = expansion
  )

# next, we will loop through each state, determining the insured population and uninsured population
for (i in 1:nrow(state_personograph)) {
  props <- list(
    "Insured" = 1 - state_personograph$uninsured_rate[i],
    "Uninsured" = state_personograph$uninsured_rate[i]
  )

  # save each personograph so we can add it to our poster
  # png(
  #   filename = paste0("images/personograph/", state_personograph$state_name[i], ".png"),
  #   width = 1000,
  #   height = 1000,
  #   res = 300
  # )

  # use the personograph library to create the visual
  # 100 icons, proportion colored is based on the uninsured rate
  personograph(props, n.icons = 100, icon.style = 6, color = list("Uninsured" = ifelse(state_personograph$expansion[i] == 1, medicaid_colors$expansion, medicaid_colors$nonexpansion), "Insured" = "gray"), plot.width = 0.95, fig.title = state_personograph$state_name[i])

  # dev.off()
}
```

# Plot: Insurance Rates by FPL

```{r}
# since we have continuous FPL data, we need group it before plotting
# groups of 10% 
bin_width <- 10

# now lets create a dataframe that contains the average uninsured rate per
# FPL group per state
fpl_coverage_df <- acs_2023 |>
  mutate(
    # creating the bins
    bin = floor(POVPIP / bin_width) * bin_width,
    # setting the value of the bin to the middle
    bin_mid = bin + bin_width / 2
  ) |>
  group_by(state_name, expansion, bin_mid) |>
  summarise(
    # calculate uninsured rate for the state/bin (using the subject weights)
    uninsured_rate = weighted.mean(uninsured, PWGTP),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # make sure the expansion status is a factor, so it uses the correct colors
    expansion = factor(expansion, levels = c(1, 0), labels = c("Expansion", "Non-Expansion"))
  )

# for this plot, we are also going to include the nationwide average uninsured rate
# this way, we can compare each states distribution of uninsurance over FPL to the national average
avg_df <- fpl_coverage_df |>
  group_by(bin_mid) |>
  summarise(
    avg_uninsured = weighted.mean(uninsured_rate, w = n),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
# now, we cna plot
# we will plot FPL % on the x axis, and uninsured rate on the y, colored by expansion status (so we can indentify
# which states expanded and which did not, and explore any trends there), and group by state so we can 
# facet wrap and plot each state individually
ggplot(fpl_coverage_df, aes(x = bin_mid, y = uninsured_rate, color = expansion, group = state_name)) +
  # state-specific
  geom_line() +
  # national average 
  geom_line(data = avg_df, aes(x = bin_mid, y = avg_uninsured, group = 1), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "gray60") +
  # threshold for medicaid eligibility after expansion 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 138, linetype = "dotted", linewidth  = 0.7, color = "gray40") +
  # 
  annotate(
    "text",
    x        = 155,
    y        = max(fpl_coverage_df$uninsured_rate, na.rm = TRUE) - 0.05,
    label    = "138% FPL",
    hjust    = 0.00,
    size     = 3.0,
    color    = "gray40",
    fontface = "italic"
  ) +
  # state-specific plots
  facet_wrap(~ state_name, scales = "fixed", ncol = 5) +
  # convert axis to percent
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1, scale = 1)) +
  # use our custom mediciad color palette
  scale_color_manual(values = medicaid_colors$expansion_state) +
  # add our axis labels and a caption for the data source
  labs(
    # title = "Uninsured Rates Across Federal Poverty Level (FPL)",
    x = "Federal Poverty Level",
    y = "Uninsured Rate",
    color = "Expansion Status",
    caption  = "Source: ACS PUMS 2023"
  ) +
  # apply our custom medicaid theme and fonts
  theme_medicaid() +
  # hide the legend (we will add our own on the poster)
  theme(
    legend.position  = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

# Plot: Nationwide DiD

```{r}
# the difference-in-difference plot, will demosntrate the change in uninsured rates
# over time. nontably, before and ACA in 2014 and the difference in changes between
# expansion and nonexpanison states
state_year_panel <- acs |> 
  # for this analysis, we are only going to focus on those under 138% (most likely to have been affected by these policy changes)
  filter(low_income == 1) |> 
  group_by(state_name, year, expansion, expansion_year) |> 
  summarise(
    uninsured_rate = weighted.mean(uninsured, as.numeric(PWGTP)),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
# now, we want to identify the pre treatment and post treatment groups (before/after 2014)
# and years relative to the date of treatment
state_year_panel_did <- state_year_panel |>
  filter(expansion_year == 2014 | is.na(expansion_year)) |>
  mutate(
    post     = ifelse(year >= 2014, 1, 0),
    year_rel = year - 2014,
    year_f   = factor(year)
  )
```

```{r}
# using the fixest library, we can build our DiD model
did_model <- feols(
  uninsured_rate ~ i(year_rel, expansion, ref = -1) | state_name + year_f,
  data = state_year_panel_did,
  cluster = ~state_name
)
```

```{r}
# extract coefficients and confidence intervals
did_coefs <- broom::tidy(did_model, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    year_rel = as.numeric(str_extract(term, "-?[0-9]+")),
    year     = year_rel + 2014
  ) |>
  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      term      = "reference",
      estimate  = 0,
      std.error = 0,
      conf.low  = 0,
      conf.high = 0,
      year_rel  = -1,
      year      = 2013
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  select(year, year_rel, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)
```

```{r}
# lets determine the national average for each group and year 
# for example, 2014 expansion, 2014 non expansion, 2015 expansion, 2015 non expansion, etc
group_avg <- state_year_panel_did |>
  group_by(year, expansion) |>
  summarise(
    avg_uninsured = weighted.mean(uninsured_rate, n, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    expansion_name = ifelse(expansion == 1, "Expansion", "Non-Expansion")
  )
```

```{r}
# now, lets calculate our counterfactuals, based on the national averages
counterfactual_df <- group_avg |>
  left_join(did_coefs, by = "year") |>
  mutate(
    counterfactual = case_when(
      # for expansion states, subtract the effect (if not expanded)
      expansion == 1 ~ avg_uninsured - estimate,
      # for nonexpansion states, add the effect (if expanded)
      expansion == 0 ~ avg_uninsured + estimate,
    ),
    actual_label = ifelse(expansion == 1, "Expansion (Actual)", "Non-Expansion (Actual)"),
    counterfactual_label = ifelse(expansion == 1, "Expansion (Without Expansion)", "Non-Expansion (With Expansion)")
  )
```

```{r}
# now lets put this information into a format we can actually use for the plot
plot_df <- counterfactual_df |>
  select(year, expansion, expansion_name, actual_label, counterfactual_label, avg_uninsured, counterfactual) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(avg_uninsured, counterfactual),
    names_to = "type",
    values_to = "uninsured_rate"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    line_label = ifelse(type == "avg_uninsured", actual_label, counterfactual_label),
    line_type = ifelse(type == "avg_uninsured", "solid", "dashed")
  )

# since we only want to show the counterfactual post treatment year
# we need to subset the data into pre / post treatment
pre_df <- plot_df |> 
  filter(year <= 2013)

post_df <- plot_df |> 
  filter(year >= 2013)

ribbon_df <- counterfactual_df |> 
  filter(year >= 2013) |> 
  select(year, expansion, expansion_name, avg_uninsured, counterfactual)
```

```{r}
# this plot will be a differnce-in-difference, showing the trend of uninsured rates
# from 2010-2023 (excluding 2020) for both expansion and nonexpansion groups
# it will also show the counterfactuals for each
ggplot() +
  # shade the area between the actual and countefactual, to highlight the difference between the two
  geom_ribbon(data = ribbon_df, aes(x = year, ymin = pmin(avg_uninsured, counterfactual), ymax = pmax(avg_uninsured, counterfactual), fill = expansion_name, group = expansion_name), alpha = 0.15) +
  # pre treatment actual line (there is no pretreatment counterfactual)
  geom_line(data = pre_df |> filter(type == "avg_uninsured"), aes(x = year, y = uninsured_rate, color = expansion_name, group = expansion_name), linewidth = 1.2) +
  # post treatment actual line
  geom_line(data = post_df |> filter(type == "avg_uninsured"), aes(x = year, y = uninsured_rate, color = expansion_name, group = expansion_name), linewidth = 1.2) +
  # post treatment counterfactual (lets make it dashed))
  geom_line(data = post_df |> filter(type == "counterfactual"), aes(x = year, y = uninsured_rate, color = expansion_name, group = expansion_name), linewidth = 0.5, linetype  = "dashed") +
  # pre and post treatment actual points (for aesthetics, and to make it clearer)
  geom_point(data = plot_df |> filter(type == "avg_uninsured"), aes(x = year, y = uninsured_rate, color = expansion_name), size = 3) +
  # # draw a vertical line at 2013, to indicate start of ACA and medicaid expansion
  # geom_vline(xintercept = 2013, linetype = "dotted", color = "gray40", linewidth  = 0.7) +
  # # adding an annotation for the vertical line, so the viewer knows that it means
  # annotate("text", x = 2013.2, y = max(plot_df$uninsured_rate, na.rm = TRUE) - 0.01, label = "ACA Expansion Begins", hjust = 0.00, size = 3.5, color = "gray40", fontface = "italic") +
  # using our own custom medicaid color palettes
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Expansion" = medicaid_colors$expansion, "Non-Expansion" = medicaid_colors$nonexpansion)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Expansion" = medicaid_colors$expansion, "Non-Expansion" = medicaid_colors$nonexpansion)) +
  # define our x axis scale
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2010:2023) +
  # convert our y axis to percent (instead of decimals)
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 0.6)) +
  # add our title, axis labels and caption
  labs(
    # title = "Effect of Medicaid Expansion on Uninsured Rates",
    # subtitle = "Solid lines = actual  |  Dashed lines = counterfactual  |  Shaded area = estimated effect",
    x = "",
    y = "Uninsured Rate",
    color = "Expansion Status",
    
    caption = "Source: ACS PUMS  |  Counterfactual estimated via Difference-in-Differences"
  ) + 
  # use our custom mediciad theme and fonts
  theme_medicaid() +
  # hide the legend (we will add our own on the poster)
  theme(
    legend.position  = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

# Plot: State-Specific DiD

```{r}
# for the state specific counterfactual plots,
# we need to first calculate the state uninsured rate for each year
state_avg <- state_year_panel |>
  group_by(state_name, year) |>
  summarise(
    uninsured_rate = weighted.mean(uninsured_rate, n, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
# we will have to repeat this for each state we want a plot for
# so lets declare it upfront and reuse the variable throghout
current_state <- "Pennsylvania"
state_expansion_year <- ifelse(is.na(expansion_years[current_state]), Inf, expansion_years[current_state])

did_coefs <- did_coefs |>
  complete(year_rel = min(year_rel):max(year_rel)) |>
  mutate(
    year = year_rel + 2014,
    estimate = zoo::na.approx(estimate, na.rm = FALSE),
    std.error = zoo::na.approx(std.error, na.rm = FALSE),
    conf.low = zoo::na.approx(conf.low, na.rm = FALSE),
    conf.high = zoo::na.approx(conf.high, na.rm = FALSE)
  ) |>
  filter(year >= 2010, year <= 2023)

# join the did coefs we calculate above to the state specific df
state_df <- state_avg |>
  filter(state_name == current_state) |>
  mutate(
    year_rel = year - state_expansion_year
  )

if (is.na(expansion_years[current_state])) {
  state_df <- state_df |> left_join(did_coefs |> select(year, estimate), by = "year")
} else {
  state_df <- state_df |> left_join(did_coefs |> select(year_rel, estimate), by = "year_rel")
}

state_df <- state_df |>
  mutate(
    counterfactual = case_when(
      is.na(expansion_years[current_state]) & year == 2013 ~ uninsured_rate,
      is.na(expansion_years[current_state]) & year <  2013 ~ NA_real_,
      is.na(expansion_years[current_state]) & year >= 2014 ~ uninsured_rate + estimate,
      year == state_expansion_year - 1 ~ uninsured_rate,
      year <  state_expansion_year - 1 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ uninsured_rate - estimate
    )
  ) |>
  select(year, uninsured_rate, counterfactual)

# add out plot labels and line type (solid or dashed) based on actual or counterfactual
plot_df <- state_df |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(uninsured_rate, counterfactual),
    names_to = "type",
    values_to = "uninsured"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    line_label = ifelse(type == "uninsured_rate", "Pennsylvania (Actual)", "Pennsylvania (If Expanded)"),
    line_type  = ifelse(type == "uninsured_rate", "solid", "dashed")
  )

split_year <- ifelse(is.na(expansion_years[current_state]), 2013, state_expansion_year - 1)

# categorize based on pre / post ACA expansion (to only show counterfactuals post expansion)
pre_df  <- plot_df |> filter(year <= split_year)
post_df <- plot_df |> filter(year >= split_year)

# create ribbon df for shading the area between actual and counterfactual
ribbon_df <- state_df |>
  filter(year >= split_year) |>
  transmute(year, actual = uninsured_rate, counterfactual)

state_color <- ifelse(
  is.na(expansion_years[current_state]),
  medicaid_colors$nonexpansion,
  medicaid_colors$expansion
)

# start our plot
ggplot() +
  # vertical ACA expansion start line (ACA expansion started in Jan 2014)
  # this is the first layer, so it is in the background, behind everything else
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = split_year,
    linetype   = "dotted",
    color      = "gray40",
    linewidth  = 0.7
  ) +
  # add pre ACA expansion solid line, actual values (no counterfactuals for the pre expansion period)
  geom_line(
    data = pre_df |> filter(type == "uninsured_rate"),
    aes(x = year, y = uninsured),
    color     = state_color,
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  # add post ACA expansion solid line, actual values
  geom_line(
    data = post_df |> filter(type == "uninsured_rate"),
    aes(x = year, y = uninsured),
    color     = state_color,
    linewidth = 1.2,
    linetype  = "solid"
  ) +
  # add post ACA expansion dashed line, counterfactual values
  geom_line(
    data = post_df |> filter(type == "counterfactual"),
    aes(x = year, y = uninsured),
    color     = state_color,
    linewidth = 0.6,
    linetype  = "dashed"
  ) +
  # add points for post ACA expansion actual values
  geom_point(
    data = plot_df |> filter(type == "uninsured_rate"),
    aes(x = year, y = uninsured),
    color = state_color,
    size  = 3
  ) +
  # add the ribbon to shade the area between actual and counterfactual
  geom_ribbon(
    data = ribbon_df,
    aes(
      x    = year,
      ymin = pmin(actual, counterfactual),
      ymax = pmax(actual, counterfactual)
    ),
    fill  = state_color,
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  # annotation for ACA expansion start vertical line
  # annotate(
  #   "text",
  #   x        = 2013.2,
  #   y        = max(plot_df$uninsured, na.rm = TRUE) - 0.01,
  #   label    = "ACA Expansion Begins",
  #   hjust    = 0.00,
  #   size     = 3.5,
  #   color    = "gray40",
  #   fontface = "italic"
  # ) +
  # adding this to ensure every year is labeled
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2010:2023) +
  # convert decimals to percent, and add upper limit of 0.6 (above the max uninsured rate, 
  # ensures all state plots are consistently formatted and comparable side-by-side)
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 0.6)) +
  # add labels and caption, years are self-explanatory so lets remove it
  labs(
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Uninsured Rate",
    caption = "Source: ACS PUMS  |  Counterfactual estimated via Difference-in-Differences"
  ) +
  # add our custom medicaid theme
  theme_medicaid() +
  # remove legend, no need here
  theme(
    legend.position  = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}
# create a df containing all the columns we need for the json
state_avg_json <- state_year_panel |>
  group_by(state_name, year, expansion, expansion_year) |>
  summarise(

# create seperate df for nonexpansion and expansion states
never_expanded_json <- state_avg_json |>
  filter(is.na(expansion_year)) |>
  left_join(did_coefs |> select(year, estimate), by = "year")

ever_expanded_json <- state_avg_json |>

# format into json usable for the website
state_df_json <- bind_rows(never_expanded_json, ever_expanded_json) |>
  mutate(
    uninsured_counterfactual = case_when(

      is.na(expansion_year) & year <  2013 ~ NA_real_,        
      is.na(expansion_year) & year >= 2014 ~ uninsured_rate + estimate,  
      year == state_expansion_year - 1     ~ uninsured_rate,       
      year <  state_expansion_year - 1     ~ NA_real_,             
      TRUE                                 ~ uninsured_rate - estimate
    )
  ) |>
  select(state_name, year, expansion, expansion_year, uninsured_rate, uninsured_counterfactual) |>
  arrange(state_name, year)
```

```{r}
# we will have to repeat this for each state
# so lets declare it upfront and reuse the variable throghout
current_state = "Massachusetts"

# first we need the population count for low income adults per state per year
# this gives us the denominator to convert rates to headcounts
state_population <- acs_2023 |>
  filter(low_income == 1) |>
  group_by(state_name, year) |>
  summarise(
    pop = sum(as.numeric(PWGTP)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# pull the selected states data
selected_state_data <- state_df_json |>
  filter(state_name == current_state)

# get 2023 data
snapshot_2023 <- selected_state_data |>
  filter(year == 2023)

# get population for headline number
selected_pop <- state_population |>
  filter(state_name == current_state, year == 2023)

# compute headline number
actual_rate <- snapshot_2023$uninsured_rate
counterfactual_rate <- snapshot_2023$uninsured_counterfactual
rate_gap <- abs(actual_rate - counterfactual_rate)
people_gap <- round(rate_gap * selected_pop$pop)
expansion_status <- !is.na(snapshot_2023$expansion_year)
state_color <- ifelse(expansion_status, medicaid_colors$expansion, medicaid_colors$nonexpansion)

# label depends on expansion status
headline_label <- ifelse(
  expansion_status,
  "people covered due to expansion (2023)",
  "people left uninsured due to non-expansion (2023)"
)

# 2023 bar data 
bar_df <- tibble(
  label = c("Actual", "Counterfactual"),
  rate  = c(actual_rate, counterfactual_rate)
)

# create the uninsured population due to expansion decision visual
ggplot() +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0.5, y = 0.7,
    label = scales::comma(people_gap),
    size = 22,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = state_color,
    hjust = 0.5
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0.5, y = 0.25,
    label = headline_label,
    size = 4.5,
    color = "gray40",
    hjust = 0.5,
    fontface = "italic"
  ) +
  # annotate(
  #   "text",
  #   x = 0.5, y = 0.05,
  #   label = current_state,
  #   size  = 5.5,
  #   color = "gray20",
  #   hjust = 0.5,
  #   fontface = "bold"
  # ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_void()

# create bar indicating percent of low income unisured for 2023
ggplot() +
  # gray background
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = 0, xmax = 1,
    ymin = 0.3, ymax = 0.7,
    fill = "gray92",
    color = NA
  ) +
  # percent of low income uninsured for 2023
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = 0,
    xmax = actual_rate,
    ymin = 0.3,
    ymax = 0.7,
    fill = state_color,
    alpha = 0.85,
    color = NA
  ) +
  # rate label inside bar
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = actual_rate / 2,
    y = 0.5,
    label = scales::percent(actual_rate, accuracy = 0.1),
    color = "white",
    size = 4.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  # format x axis as percent instead of fraction
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  # y axis should fill the height of the bar
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  # main label / title
  labs(x = "Uninsured Rate (2023)", y = NULL) +
  # apply custom themes
  theme_medicaid() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```
